item.title: Slipped hazard and property damage from street tree berry drop, 8th August
item.description:
There is an ongoing safety hazard and a property damage issue caused by a council street tree planted directly outside my property near the junction of Warwick Road (N18). The tree produces a high volume of berries that fall heavily onto the public footway. As pedestrians step on these berries, they smash into a slick, sticky residue, creating an imminent slip risk on the pavement directly outside my home. I have tried to sweep up the fallen berries myself to maintain the path; however, because they smash instantly upon hitting the floor, sweeping is completely ineffective against the stubborn, stained residue left behind. Furthermore, this crushed berry residue adheres aggressively to footwear. It is unavoidably tracked directly into my vehicle and my house, causing persistent staining and damage to carpets and flooring. I kindly request that the Council’s arboricultural team inspect this tree for remedial action, such as significant pruning to reduce fruit yields or replacing the specimen with a non-fruiting alternative.

Nearest address to the pin placed on the map (from OS Places API): Warwick Road, Edmonton
Report on FixMyStreet
